questions.problem:
Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}].
$$

A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,-1),(1,1),$ and $(3,2).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under the action of $T?$

- $(-1,4)$
- $(-2,4)$
- $(1,-3)$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the image of $S$ under the action of $T$, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under $T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 & 1 \\ 4 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are  $(-2,4)$, and $(1,-2).$ 

So, the correct answer is " II only."

T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 6 & 2\end{aligned}].

So, the correct answer is "II and III only."

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062587/assets/e6d0ce147aec90c3840a893e36596fbadf981ff96559f65d055f4486406cca7f.png)

Consider the linear transformation $T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

What would be the image of the quadrilateral shown above under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $T$ with associated $2\times 2$ matrix $T,$ we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $T$ is non-singular, i.e., $det(T)\ne 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $T$ is singular, i.e., $det(T)=0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $T$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $T$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is the point $(0,0),$ the origin of the coordinate system.

With that in mind, let's examine our transformation.

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}det(T) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-1\cdot 1-0\cdot 1 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a nonsingular matrix. Therefore, the image of our object under the action of  $T$ is a quadrilateral.

choices.value: The origin $O$ of the coordinate system
A point, different from the origin

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062587/assets/95c80fe2654c8f6eb4b65492eab1efb07f568375b2960b1633e5e2e1a7741a8b.png)
Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the action of $\mathbf T$ by calculating the matrix product $TX\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}TX & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ -6 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -6 & -2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the image's vertices are $(3,-6), (1,-2),$ and $(-2,4).$  Notice that all three points lie on the same line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062587/assets/3fd1073b2eaa5aa9c21e537fcc4dc6cf538ab2992c0732f64da50dbcb63d8fd4.png)

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Identifying the Type of Image Formed by a Linear Transformation
canonical_examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062587/assets/89efcd0ecb51dac08a1102c5a347eea3459f7209de7cbac0a88b192259ca3b7e.png)

Consider the linear transformation $\mathbf T$ with matrix representation $T,$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14062587/assets/501ab476f0e420892fee6c87307dd33f260affc1533019621b366b5462920322.png)
What would be the image of the triangle shown above under the action of $\mathbf{T}?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with associated $2 \times 2$ matrix $T,$ we have one of the following three possibilities:

- If $\mathbf{T}$ is non-singular, i.e., $\det(T) \neq 0,$ then the image of a two-dimensional object is a two-dimensional object. In particular, the image of a polygon with $n$ vertices is a polygon with $n$ vertices.

- If $\mathbf{T}$ is singular, i.e., $\det(T) = 0,$ we have two additional subcases:

- If $T$ has at least one nonzero entry, then the image of a two-dimensional object is a one-dimensional line segment.

- If $T$ is the zero matrix, then the image of a two-dimensional object is the point $(0,0),$ the origin of the coordinate system.

Since $T$ is the zero matrix, the image of our object under the action of $\mathbf{T}$ is the origin.
